title: Rapid hire + price experimentation 12-week microforecast
executive_summary: Working spreadsheet for a short, measurable program pairing rapid contractor hires with targeted enterprise price tilts. Objective: test which mix preserves runway while minimizing SLA and churn risk; produce a 12-week rolling forecast and clear pilot triggers.
assumptions: Starting runway (today): 8.6 months based on Sep-2026 run rate
Engineering fully-burdened monthly cost per FTE: $26,500
Small-customer price elasticity: -0.15 to -0.4 depending on slab sensitivity
Enterprise slab cohorts represent ~42% of ARR but only 18% of call volume
Price tilt windows tested: +4%, +9%, +15% applied to targeted enterprise slabs
Recruiting lead time for contractor conversion: 2-5 weeks
Operational lever: enable auto-fallback to quantized model variants to reclaim ~1.2 FTE equiv throughput per 100k QPS for affected routes

sensitivity_analysis_notes: Top sensitivities from the 12-week Monte Carlo runs: (1) Small-customer elasticity dominates near-term revenue; a +4% tilt yields median -7% volume for that cohort with long tail recovery. (2) Hiring cadence matters: front-loaded hires create largest short-term burn; spreading over 6 weeks reduces peak burn by ~35%. (3) Operational substitution (quantized fallback) materially reduces SLA risk and is most effective for read-heavy routes. (4) Customer churn shows threshold behavior: once perceived cost or latency crosses a cohort-specific tolerance, crediting programs are required to avoid >2% ARR loss for affected accounts.
